sanskrit:
ध्यायतो विषयान्पुंसः सङ्गस्तेषूपजायते।
सङ्गात् संजायते कामः कामात्क्रोधोऽभिजायते।।
image_english: Thinking of objects leads to attachment; attachment breeds desire; unfulfilled desire creates anger.
caption:
Chapter 2, Verse 62

Kṛṣṇa describes the ‘Ladder of Fall’—the psychological chain reaction that leads to destruction. It starts innocently: ‘dhyāyato viṣayān puṁsaḥ’ (While contemplating the objects of the senses). You just think about it. Then ‘saṅgas teṣūpajāyate’ (attachment develops). You feel you need it. From attachment comes ‘kāmaḥ’ (lust/intense desire). If that desire is thwarted, ‘krodho ’bhijāyate’ (anger arises). This verse warns us that the battlefield is in the mind. The moment you let your mind dwell on a sense object, you have stepped onto a slippery slope. A spiritualist must catch the mind at the stage of ‘contemplation’ (dhyāyato) before it snowballs into lust and anger. Prevention is better than cure.
